title: The European Union
objective: After this level you can explain how the EU works.
summary: The EU began with six countries pooling coal and steel to make war impossible. Today 27 members share lawmaking: the Commission proposes; Parliament and Council adopt.

cards.headline: It started with coal, steel and a plan to make war impossible.
cards.body: On 9 May 1950, French foreign minister Robert Schuman proposed pooling Western Europe's coal and steel industries. His aim was to make war between France and Germany "not merely unthinkable, but materially impossible." Today's European Union grew from that idea.

cards.context: Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands signed a treaty to run their coal and steel industries jointly, so no single country could make the weapons of war to turn against the others. The goal was to end the bloody conflicts that had culminated in the Second World War. That first step led to today's European Union of 27 countries.

cards.headline: Laws made in a triangle
cards.body: Everything the EU does rests on treaties its member countries agreed to voluntarily and democratically. Lawmaking runs through a triangle. The European Commission proposes a law. Two bodies adopt it: the European Parliament, directly elected by EU citizens, and the Council of the EU, where ministers from each member government sit. The member countries then put it into practice, and the Commission checks that they do.

cards.headline: Sharing the final say
cards.body: Remember Level 81: sovereignty means having the final say. EU members agreed, by treaty, to make some of their laws together, through a Parliament and a Council they all share, instead of each deciding alone. The final say hasn't vanished: in treaties they chose to sign, the members agreed to share some of it.

cards.headline: The EU: explained
learned: Schuman (1950): pool coal and steel to end war
Six countries went first in 1951; today there are 27
Commission proposes; Parliament and Council adopt
Members agreed by treaty to decide some laws together

questions.prompt: Which industries did the six founding countries first agree to run together?

options.label: Oil and gas
options.rationale: Not oil and gas: the plan named coal and steel.

options.label: Farming and fishing
options.rationale: Those came later; the first step was coal and steel.

questions.explanation: Schuman proposed pooling coal and steel, and six countries signed a treaty to run them jointly in 1951.

questions.prompt: In the EU's lawmaking triangle, what is the European Commission's role?

options.label: It is directly elected by EU citizens
It seats ministers from each member government
options.rationale: That's the Council of the EU.

options.label: It alone adopts every EU law
options.rationale: Laws are adopted by the Parliament and the Council.

questions.explanation: The Commission proposes new laws; the Parliament and the Council adopt them.

questions.prompt: Level 41's laws need both chambers to agree. Which two EU bodies adopt EU laws?

options.label: The European Commission and the Council of the EU
options.rationale: The Commission proposes laws; it doesn't adopt them.

options.label: The European Parliament and the European Commission
options.rationale: The Commission proposes; Parliament and the Council adopt.

options.label: The European Parliament and the Council of the EU
The member countries' own parliaments, all 27
options.rationale: Member countries put EU laws into practice.

questions.explanation: Like two chambers agreeing a bill, the directly elected European Parliament and the Council of ministers both adopt the laws the Commission proposes.
